issues.title: Site pooling uses a fixed site list
issues.summary: The specification lists pooled sites instead of expressing the SAP page 10 pooling algorithm.
issues.expected: Pool sites with fewer than 3 patients in any treatment group, combine a still-small pool with the next fewest-enrolling site, and break ties at random.
issues.observed: The specification maps seven fixed site IDs ('702','706','707','711','714','715','717') to the pool; it states no repeat-pooling or tie-break rule.
issues.action: Replace the fixed list with the documented algorithm, or document and justify the fixed assignment.

citations.quote: Sites that enroll fewer than 3 patients in any one treatment group will be grouped together
then this group of patients will be combined with the next fewest enrolling site
In the event that there is a tie for fewest-enrolling site, one of these will be chosen at random by a random-number generator.

issues.title: First-dose date uses a different source
issues.summary: Define-XML names the Visit 3 date; the specification reads the earliest exposure start date.
issues.expected: Define-XML: SV.SVSTDTC when SV.VISITNUM=3. SAP page 16: the date of first dose [Week 0 (Visit 3) unless indicated otherwise].
issues.observed: The specification uses MIN(EX.EXSTDTC). The adjudicator disputes the SAP comparison, since the SAP names the first dose; the Define-XML difference stands.
issues.action: Confirm the intended source and align the Define-XML comment and the specification.

citations.quote: the date of first dose [Week 0 (Visit 3) unless indicated otherwise]

issues.title: First-dose date imputation is undocumented
issues.summary: The specification fills missing month and day components with 1; no retained document states an imputation rule for TRTSDT.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT converts the first-dose date to a SAS date and states no partial-date completion.
issues.observed: The specification completes partial dates with month 1 and day 1.
issues.action: Confirm and document the completion policy, or remove the unsupported imputation.

issues.title: Last-dose fallback omits the discontinued-after-Visit-3 condition
issues.summary: Define-XML uses the discontinuation date only for subjects who discontinued after Visit 3; the specification applies it whenever the last dose date is missing.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADSL.TRTEDT: use the discontinuation date when the last dose date is missing and the subject discontinued after visit 3.
issues.observed: The specification takes DS_DISP.DSSTDTC whenever the final exposure end date is missing, with no visit condition.
issues.action: Add the documented condition, or document why a broader fallback is intended.

citations.quote: and the subject discontinued after visit 3

issues.title: Last-dose date imputation is undocumented
issues.summary: Partial last-dose and fallback discontinuation dates are completed without a documented ADSL rule.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADSL.TRTEDT states the source, a conditional fallback and conversion to a SAS date, with no partial-date completion.
issues.observed: Both branches fill missing month and day components with 1.
issues.action: Confirm and document the imputation policy, or remove the unsupported completion.

issues.title: Zero-duration guard may need no separate rule
issues.summary: The check flags NULLIF(TRTDUR, 0) as undocumented; the adjudicator disputes that it changes the documented division.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADSL.AVGDD: CUMDOSE/TRTDUR, which has no value in SAS when TRTDUR is zero.
issues.observed: The specification makes the missing result explicit with NULLIF(TRTDUR, 0); the adjudicator considers this equivalent.
issues.action: Resolve the disputed check; if the guard is equivalent, close it without a documentation change.

issues.title: Cumulative dose sums exposure records instead of planned doses
issues.summary: Define-XML computes planned dose over visit intervals; the specification sums recorded EX doses over exposure days.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE: CUMDOSE=TRT01PN*TRTDUR, and for high dose 54mg per day for the days in the 1st dosing interval, with visit 4 and visit 12 boundaries.
issues.observed: The specification computes SUM(EX.EXDOSE * (EX.EXENDY - EX.EXSTDY + 1)) without the documented visit-interval branches.
issues.action: Agree the intended calculation and align Define-XML and the specification.

citations.quote: 54mg per day for the # of days subj was in 1st dosing interval

issues.title: Open-ended exposure is extended to TRTEDT without a rule
issues.summary: An exposure record without an end date is extended to TRTEDT; no retained document mentions EX records or that extension.
issues.expected: State how a final exposure record with a missing end date contributes to cumulative dose.
issues.observed: The specification adds _DOSE0 * _DAYS0, the dose of the open-ended record through TRTEDT.
issues.action: Document the extension rule or revise the computation.

issues.title: Age group is derived from AGE instead of AGEGR1N (disputed)
issues.summary: Define-XML derives AGEGR1 from AGEGR1N; the specification derives it from AGE directly.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADSL.AGEGR1: derived from ADSL.AGEGR1N, whose cutpoints are AGE <65, 65-80 and >80.
issues.observed: The specification tests DM.AGE < 65 and the other cutpoints; the adjudicator considers the reversed order the same categorization.
issues.action: Resolve the disputed equivalence before requiring a specification change.

issues.title: Numeric age group is derived from AGEGR1 instead of AGE (disputed)
issues.summary: Define-XML derives AGEGR1N from AGE cutpoints; the specification maps it from the character group AGEGR1.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADSL.AGEGR1N: 1 if AGE <65, 2 if AGE 65-80, 3 if AGE >80.
issues.observed: The specification takes AGEGR1N from AGEGR1; the adjudicator finds the composed rule states the same cutpoints and codes.
issues.action: Resolve the disputed equivalence before requiring a specification change.

citations.quote: AGEGR1 = 1 if AGE <65. AGEGR1 = 2 if AGE 65-80. AGEGR1 = 3 if AGE >80.

issues.title: Race mapping omits ASIAN
issues.summary: Define-XML codes ASIAN as 7, but the specification RACEN mapping has no ASIAN entry.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADSL.RACEN: 7 = ASIAN.
issues.observed: The specification maps no ASIAN value, so an ASIAN subject would get a missing RACEN.
issues.action: Add the documented ASIAN = 7 mapping.

issues.title: Completer definitions disagree on population
issues.summary: SAP page 9 restricts Week 24 completers to the efficacy population; the Define-XML COMP24FL rule does not.
issues.expected: SAP page 9: all patients in the efficacy population who completed their Week 24 visit (Visit 12).
issues.observed: Define-XML ADSL.COMP24FL: Y if subject has a SV.VISITNUM=12 and ENDDT>= date of visit 12, with no efficacy-population condition.
issues.action: Confirm whether completers must be in the efficacy population and align the SAP, Define-XML and specification.

citations.quote: Y if subject has a SV.VISITNUM=12 and ENDDT>= date of visit 12
All patients in the efficacy population who completed their Week 24 visit (Visit 12).

issues.title: Published BMI formula multiplies height by 100 instead of dividing
issues.summary: Define-XML multiplies height by 100; the specification and Pilot 6 adsl.r divide height in cm by 100, as kg/m^2 requires.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADSL.BMIBL: WEIGHTBL / ((HEIGHTBL*100)**2), 1 significant digit.
issues.observed: The formula as written differs from the reference on 253 of 254 records (values near 0); dividing height by 100 reproduces all 254, as adsl.r L253 does.
issues.action: Confirm metres were intended and correct the Define-XML formula to WEIGHTBL / ((HEIGHTBL/100)**2).

issues.title: Obese category code differs from the codelist
issues.summary: Codelist BMICAT codes the obese group as >30; reference and output store >=30. The numeric cutoff BMI >=30 agrees across Define-XML and the SAP.
issues.expected: Define-XML codelist BMICAT: <25 = Normal; 25-<30 = Overweight; >30 = Obese. SAP pages 13 and 22: BMI>=30, obese(>=30).
issues.observed: The reference holds 28 >=30 values outside codelist BMICAT. The adjudicator disputes the two boundary contradictions: >30 is the code, not the cutoff.
issues.action: Align the obese code in codelist BMICAT and the data, keeping the documented BMI >=30 boundary.

issues.title: Missing baseline BMI is assigned to the <25 group
issues.summary: Define-XML and SAP page 10 leave a subject without baseline BMI ungrouped; the specification and reference assign <25.
issues.expected: Define-XML: Normal if . < BMIBL <25, so a missing BMI has no group. SAP page 10: missing baseline values will not be imputed.
issues.observed: The literal rule differs on 29 of 254: 28 are the >=30 code (separate issue), 1 is subject 01-702-1082 with no BMIBL, put in <25. The SAS-comparison reading is disputed.
issues.action: Decide whether a missing BMIBL has no group or <25, then align Define-XML, the specification and the reference.

citations.quote: Missing baseline values and missing safety data will not be imputed
BMIBLGR1=Normal if . < BMIBL <25. BMIBLGR1=Overweight if 25 <=BMIBL <30. BMIBLGR1=Obese if BMIBL >=30
SAS Version 9.2 was used for the generation of ADaM datasets and analysis displays.

issues.title: Baseline height has no Visit 1 restriction
issues.summary: Define-XML takes height at Visit 1; the specification takes the earliest HEIGHT record at any visit.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADSL.HEIGHTBL: VS.VSTESTCD='HEIGHT' and VS.VISITNUM=1.
issues.observed: The specification keeps the earliest HEIGHT record by VISITNUM without restricting the visit, so it can select another visit.
issues.action: Add the documented Visit 1 restriction or document the intended fallback.

issues.title: Baseline weight uses the baseline flag instead of Visit 3
issues.summary: Define-XML takes weight at Visit 3; the specification selects the record flagged VSBLFL=Y.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADSL.WEIGHTBL: VS.VSTESTCD='WEIGHT' and VS.VISITNUM=3.
issues.observed: The specification filters VS.VSBLFL = 'Y' without VISITNUM=3; no retained document equates the two selections.
issues.action: Confirm whether the baseline flag or Visit 3 defines the intended record.

issues.title: Documented education test code YEARSEDU matches no records
issues.summary: Define-XML names SCTESTCD=YEARSEDU; the staged SC data, the specification and Pilot 6 adsl.r use EDLEVEL.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADSL.EDUCLVL: SC.SCSTRESN where SC.SCTESTCD=YEARSEDU.
issues.observed: No SC record has YEARSEDU, so the literal rule differs on all 254 records; EDLEVEL, as in the specification and adsl.r L258, reproduces all 254.
issues.action: Confirm EDLEVEL as the intended test code and correct the Define-XML comment.

issues.title: Disease-duration end dates conflict within the SAP
issues.summary: SAP page 13 measures disease duration to Visit 1; page 22 measures it to enrollment, which page 9 places at Visit 3.
issues.expected: One documented end date for the duration from disease onset.
issues.observed: SAP page 13: months between date of Week -2 (Visit 1) and date of onset. SAP page 22: months between date of enrollment and date of onset.
issues.action: Agree the intended end date and align the SAP statements, Define-XML and the specification.

computed as months between date of enrollment and date of onset

issues.title: Disease-duration month calculation is unspecified
issues.summary: The documents state months between dates without a conversion or day-count rule; the specification counts both end days and divides by 30.4375.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS: number of months between VISIT1DT and DISONSET, 1 significant digit; no month convention or inclusivity is stated.
issues.observed: The specification divides an inclusive day count by 30.4375; Pilot 6 adsl.r L301-L309 uses admiral months with add_one. The documented rule is not probed.
issues.action: Document the month convention, day counting and rounding, then align the specification.

citations.quote: number of months between VISIT1DT and DISONSET

issues.title: End-of-treatment rule is misspelled and omits early terminations
issues.summary: The Define-XML VISNUMEN comment reads only 'PROTCOL COMPLETED' records; its label and the SAP include early termination, and the specification uses every disposition event.
issues.expected: SAP page 10: the Week 24 visit or early termination visit. SAP pages 17 and 40: the last visit on or before the Week 24 visit. Label: Vis 12 or Early Term.
issues.observed: The literal rule differs on 254 of 254 records; spelling PROTOCOL still leaves 144. The on-or-before-Week-24 reading and adsl.r last-SV reading reproduce all 254.
issues.action: Rewrite the Define-XML comment with the correct term, covering early terminations and the Week 24 limit.

citations.quote: if DS.VISITNUM=13 where DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED' then VISNUMEN=12, otherwise VISNUMEN=DS.VISITNUM where DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED'
end of treatment (last visit on or before Week 24 visit)
Week 24 visit or early termination visit

issues.action: Document the complete mapping, including the I/E Not Met source, so the rule can be reproduced independently.

I/E Not Met = I/E Not Met

issues.title: MMSE total sums a different result variable
issues.summary: Define-XML sums the original result QSORRES with no conversion rule; the specification sums the standardized numeric result QSSTRESN.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADSL.MMSETOT: sum of QS.QSORRES values for the subject, with no questionnaire scope or text-to-number rule.
issues.observed: The specification sums QS.QSSTRESN. The literal QSORRES rule is not probed; Pilot 6 adsl.r L316-L320 converts QSORRES to numbers and drops missing results.
issues.action: Confirm the intended result variable and, for QSORRES, its scope and conversion; align Define-XML and the specification.

citations.quote: sum of QS.QSORRES values for the subject
